messages:
incident-bot: paging: high-severity alert for gpu-queue-growth in us-west2. queue length for inference-pool-spot >= 1200, p99 latency > 2.5s, autoscaler failing to provision new spot GPUs (quota/insufficient capacity). Paging oncall @oncall and @sre-runner. Please ack.

alex.k: acked. I'm on it, pulling autoscaler logs and recent scale events.

sam.t: oncall shifting to me in 5m if needed, ping if you want handoff.

lia.m: customer impact: several hosted API customers reporting 503s and heavy token generation latency. Support has an incident banner. @support-ops please prepare external comms.

oncall: joining bridge. initial glance: autoscaler returns "InsufficientCapacity: no matching preemptible GPU instances" repeatedly. Fallback pool (dedicated-gpu-small) is at 85% usage, can't absorb full surge.

alex.k: copying autoscaler snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:04:21Z autoscaler: scaleUp: desired=60 current=42 reason="insufficient capacity: preemptible GPUs unavailable"
2026-03-15T12:04:52Z autoscaler: retry provisioning, error=QuotaExceeded
```

lia.m: estimated affected requests: ~18% of hosted-inference RPS in us-west2. Some tenants fall back to regional routing but many are pinned to us-west2.

sre-runner: quick mitigation options: 1) force-scale dedicated pool up by 30 GPUs, 2) enable cross-region failover to eu-west1 for non-PHI traffic, 3) convert some spot nodegroups to on-demand until capacity normalizes.

alex.k: trying option 1 now — scaling dedicated pool with infra API. Running:
```bash
# increase dedicated pool replicas by 6 nodes (5 GPUs each)
infractl pools scale --name dedicated-gpu-large --region us-west2 --replicas 12
```

dev-platform-bot: command accepted, starting provisioning 6 nodes in dedicated-gpu-large (us-west2). Estimated provisioning 7-9m.

sam.t: while that comes up, we can reduce queue pressure by temporarily lowering max-concurrency on lower-tier routes and enabling aggressive batching TTL. Lia, can you ask product to flip throttles?

lia.m: done. Reduced max-concurrency for free-tier routes to 2 and enabled batching TTL=100ms. Monitoring effects.

support-ops: posting incident banner to status page and opening a support triage channel for affected enterprise accounts. Draft message ready, waiting on final impact numbers.

oncall: autoscaler still shows failures for spot groups, but we see dedicated pool scaling events in cloud console. Also noticed preemption spike in the spot market — many preemptible GPUs reclaimed by provider ~5m ago.

alex.k: quick test: requeued 100 requests to dedicated pool, p99 has dropped from 2.6s to 1.1s for those. So routing to dedicated will help.

sre-runner: can we enable immediate routing policy to prefer dedicated-gpu-large for high-priority customers? That avoids cross-region latency.

dev-platform-bot: updating routing policy: setting rule priority for enterprise_tier -> dedicated-gpu-large, deploy in 15s.

lia.m: routing change applied. Observed reduction in failed requests for enterprise customers. Non-enterprise still seeing failures.

oncall: next step: if we still have sustained queue growth after dedicated pool is fully up, we'll convert one spot nodegroup to on-demand (temporary) — that requires a manual runbook approval. Do we have signoff?

sam.t: I approve; we're escalating to infra lead for cost signoff. @alex.k loop in finance for temporary spend.

alex.k: pinged finance. Also spinning a short-lived nodegroup with on-demand GPUs in us-west2 as capacity buffer. Command:
```bash
# provision small on-demand pool
infractl pools create --name ondemand-burst --region us-west2 --type on-demand --gpus 4 --replicas 3 --ttl 1h
```

dev-platform-bot: ondemand-burst creation initiated, resources requested.

lia.m: metrics: queue length dropped from 1250 -> 700 after dedicated scaling started, and to 420 after routing and on-demand buffer. Error rate for hosted API from 18% -> 4% for affected tenants.

support-ops: sent initial customer note to top 10 affected accounts. Waiting for guidance on next update cadence.

oncall: good progress. Still: need follow-ups: - investigate why autoscaler couldn't provision spot (provider-side scarcity vs quota) - improve fallback automation so dedicated pool can take traffic faster - add a circuit-breaker to prevent single region saturation from escalating - verify AB test rollouts that pinned models to spot-only variants.

sre-runner: collecting autoscaler traces and opening a bug: "autoscaler: insufficient-capacity handling, no automated fallthrough to dedicated". Adding priority=high.

alex.k: adding a post-incident mitigation item: add configurable immediate-failover threshold: if queue_len > 800 and spot_scale_retries > 3 => promote routing to dedicated automatically.

lia.m: agreed. Also propose increasing warm standby dedicated capacity by +10% during business hours.

support-ops: next customer update in 30m; current status: partial mitigation, degraded service for some non-enterprise customers, enterprise routes restored via dedicated.

oncall: handing off to @sam.t to continue post-mitigation follow-ups and RCA. I'm going offline in 10. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam.t: ack. I'll run the RCA and coordinate infra change approval. Creating follow-up thread and assigning owners.

incident-bot: incident resolved? status=mitigated, reason="dedicated scaling + on-demand buffer + routing change". Please label postmortem needed.

sam.t: opening postmortem ticket and will schedule a 30m sync with infra and SREs.

lia.m: leaving notes for follow-up: telemetry gaps (per-tenant routing visibility), autoscaler retry/backoff tuning, playbook update for spot-drains.

support-ops: closing immediate customer comms loop; will escalate any enterprise requests to account teams.

sre-runner: saving logs and traces to incident bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/2249975310/autoscaler-logs.tar.gz

sam.t: last check: p99 latency back to baseline for enterprise and decreased for other tiers; marking last_message_ts=2249975435.

incident-bot: incident thread closed for now. If any regression, reopen thread.
